text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The annual streetball festival took place in Riga in at the week-end. The game between the of Cabinet and MPs ended in a draw.
- Latvia's population has fallen by 188,000 over the past six years. At the start of 1997 there was 2,480,000 people living in Latvia, seven percent less than in 1989.
- The heads of custom offices of the Baltic states met in Tallinn and agreed to intensify cooperation.
- The professional training centre for the unemployed will open today in Riga.

- The controlling interest of the Riga carriage plant was sold at a Latvian Privatization Agency (LPA) auction to Latek for 16.060 million lats. It was the highest price ever offered at an LPA auction.
- The Riga District court sentenced alleged gangster Ivan Haritonov to three years in prison but the court released him because he has served the time.
- The board of state-owned company Latvian Railway signed an agreement with Varner Hakon Invest to lease the Riga Central railway station for 30 years.
- A World Bank mission arrives in Latvia Monday to evaluate the progress of its programmes in the country.
